def annotate_diff_lines(diff_text: str) -> str:
    """Annotate unified diff with post-image line numbers.

    Prepends a bracket tag to each content line so the reviewer can read
    the line number instead of computing it from hunk headers.  File
    headers (``---``, ``+++``, extended headers like ``rename from``)
    pass through unchanged.

    Format:
        [   79]  context line
        [+  82] +added line
        [----] -removed line (no post-image number -- deleted lines
            have no target-side line number in unified diff)
        [    ]  special marker (e.g. ``\\ No newline at end of file``)

    Returns *diff_text* unchanged on empty, None, or unparseable input.
    """
    if not diff_text or not diff_text.strip():
        return diff_text or ""

    try:
        patchset = unidiff.PatchSet(diff_text)
    except unidiff.errors.UnidiffParseError:
        return diff_text

    out: list[str] = []
    file_count = 0
    for pf in patchset:
        file_count += 1
        # Build standard git diff headers.  unidiff's source_file/
        # target_file may be /dev/null for added/removed files;
        # replace with a/ b/ prefixed paths for the diff --git line.
        src_raw = pf.source_file or "a/%s" % pf.path
        tgt_raw = pf.target_file or "b/%s" % pf.path
        src = "a/%s" % pf.path if src_raw == "/dev/null" else src_raw
        tgt = "b/%s" % pf.path if tgt_raw == "/dev/null" else tgt_raw
        out.append("diff --git %s %s" % (src, tgt))
        if pf.is_rename:
            # Rename with possible content changes: emit similarity
            # only when the file has no hunks (pure rename).
            hunks = list(pf)
            if not hunks:
                out.append("similarity index 100%")
            out.append("rename from %s" % src.removeprefix("a/"))
            out.append("rename to %s" % tgt.removeprefix("b/"))
            if hunks:
                out.append("--- %s" % src)
                out.append("+++ %s" % tgt)
                _annotate_hunks(out, hunks)
            continue
        elif pf.is_added_file:
            mode = _extract_file_mode(diff_text, pf.path, "new")
            out.append("new file mode %s" % mode)
            out.append("--- /dev/null")
            out.append("+++ %s" % tgt)
        elif pf.is_removed_file:
            mode = _extract_file_mode(diff_text, pf.path, "deleted")
            out.append("deleted file mode %s" % mode)
            out.append("--- %s" % src)
            out.append("+++ /dev/null")
        else:
            out.append("--- %s" % src)
            out.append("+++ %s" % tgt)
        _annotate_hunks(out, pf)
    if file_count == 0:
        return diff_text
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def _extract_file_mode(
    diff_text: str, filepath: str, kind: str
) -> str:
    """Extract file mode from raw diff text for *filepath*.

    *kind* is ``"new"`` or ``"deleted"``.  Returns ``"100644"`` on
    any parse failure (safe default).
    """
    import re

    pattern = r"%s file mode (\d{6})" % kind
    # Find the diff --git line for this file, then search forward
    # for the mode line (which appears after the diff --git header).
    marker = "diff --git"
    needle = " b/%s\n" % filepath
    pos = diff_text.find(needle)
    if pos < 0:
        # Try without trailing newline (end of string).
        needle = " b/%s" % filepath
        pos = diff_text.find(needle)
    if pos < 0:
        return "100644"
    # Search forward from the diff --git line for the mode line.
    # The mode line appears within ~3 lines after diff --git.
    end = min(pos + 200, len(diff_text))
    chunk = diff_text[pos:end]
    m = re.search(pattern, chunk)
    return m.group(1) if m else "100644"
